rawFindings.title: Incorrect Windows absolute path check with forward slashes not recognized
rawFindings.explanation: The isAbsolute function was changed to no longer recognize 'C:/' style paths as absolute on Windows because it removed the check for '/' following the drive letter colon (':' === path[1] && ('\' === path[2] || '/' === path[2]) became only '\' === path[2]). This breaks detection of absolute Windows paths using forward slashes.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the previous condition to allow recognition of 'C:/...' as an absolute path by changing line 70 back to: if (':' === path[1] && ('\\' === path[2] || '/' === path[2])) return true;

rawFindings.title: Incorrect Windows absolute path detection on paths with forward slashes
rawFindings.explanation: The original line that checked Windows absolute paths considered both backslash '\\' and forward slash '/' as valid path separators after a drive letter (e.g., 'C:\' or 'C:/'). The change removes the check for forward slashes, causing paths like 'C:/' to be treated incorrectly as not absolute, breaking Windows path detection where forward slashes are used.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the previous condition to allow both backslash and forward slash in Windows absolute path detection: change line 70 back to `if (':' === path[1] && ('\\' === path[2] || '/' === path[2])) return true;`.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect Windows absolute path check in utils.isAbsolute
rawFindings.explanation: The updated code removes the check for forward slash after the drive letter, considering only backslash as a valid Windows absolute path separator. This change breaks detection of valid Windows absolute paths that use forward slashes, e.g. 'C:/path'.
rawFindings.suggestion:
Restore the check for both '\\' and '/' as valid characters following the drive letter in Windows paths, i.e., change line 70 back to:
if (':' === path[1] && ('\\' === path[2] || '/' === path[2])) return true;
